page.headline: I build the systems that
page.intro: I turn product requests into prioritized work, give coding agents a test-first plan, and use the results to improve the next run.
page.description: Andrew Hyte's resume for the Qualified Software Factory team at Salesforce, featuring Atlas Builder at Fishbowl.

summary: AI-native engineer and Principal Enterprise AI Architect with 10+ years in software engineering. I design the systems coding agents use to write and verify software, from refining product requests and prioritizing tickets to test-driven development, automated QA, and GitLab pipelines. I led Atlas Builder into production at Fishbowl and designed it so support, product, and QA could start fixes from Slack.

highlights.title: Atlas Builder
highlights.description: I designed Builder so a support tech, product manager, or QA engineer could move a fix forward directly. In production for Drive frontend repos, it takes Jira work from Slack through isolated execution, testing, and agent review to a draft GitLab merge request. Engineers review and merge the change.

highlights.title: Slack integration
highlights.description: I led the design of Atlas Gateway’s Slack tools, with per-user OAuth and encrypted token storage. I also led development of Slack cards for people to approve, reject, or edit proposed agent actions. The cards work in development, and the integration includes rich link previews and Canvas support.

highlights.title: Context Sherpa
highlights.description: I started a shared toolkit that gives Claude Code access to Jira, GitLab, and other engineering tools. In March 2026, it supported a bug fix from a Slack report through ticket creation, agent code review, preview QA, and merge.

roles.title: Principal Enterprise AI Architect
responsibilities: Designed Atlas Builder so support, product, and QA could initiate fixes from Slack without waiting for engineering intake. Engineers retain review and merge authority.
Led the production rollout for Fishbowl's Drive frontend repositories. Builder starts from a Jira ticket, asks for decisions in the Slack thread, and returns a draft GitLab merge request.
Designed a pluggable Claude Code harness that takes scoped tickets through test-first planning, agent implementation, automated testing, independent review, and remediation.
Designed resource-limited Kubernetes jobs that provision repositories and toolchains per step. Routed Git clones through a proxy that supplies repository credentials server-side.

Shipped Slack run updates, structured failure details, audit events, and per-step model usage and cost tracking. Use failed runs to improve the instructions, context, and verification that guide the next run.
Used telemetry from 1,925 Atlas chat turns to guide a step-limit change and added a visible notice for users when a turn reaches its limit.
Led development of interactive Slack approval cards. In development, reviewers can approve, reject, or edit proposed agent actions in Slack. Added rich link previews and Canvas support.
Led the Atlas build-versus-buy evaluation and secured leadership approval for a shared MCP gateway with scoped access and approval gates.

roles.title: Principal AI Engineer
responsibilities: Led the tooling behind a March 2026 AI-triaged bug fix. Claude turned a Slack report into a Jira ticket, fixed the bug, and opened a GitLab merge request. An agent reviewed the code and QA validated it in a preview environment before merge.
Brought Sherpa's Slack tools into Atlas Gateway as an MCP provider, with per-user Slack OAuth and encrypted token storage. Packaged repository instructions and reusable skills for engineering and QA.

roles.title: Software Engineering Manager
responsibilities: Started Context Sherpa, a toolkit with guided setup for Claude Code to work across Jira and GitLab. The project grew to five contributors.
Led the cloud engineering team and technical roadmap, partnering with Product and Design and mentoring engineers through code reviews.

roles.title: Senior Software Engineer
responsibilities: Architected a single-spa micro-frontend platform unifying React and Angular applications while preserving independent deployments.
Led engineering migrations from Windsurf to Cursor to Claude Code. Led the winning team in Fishbowl’s Applied AI Hackathon, building a conversational agent and MCP server in two days.

roles.title: Lead Software Engineer, Frontend
responsibilities: Led five frontend engineers and weekly releases for a B2B conversational AI portal, including a no-code Canvas editor for chatbot reply flows.
Built the CI/CD pipeline with Vite, Netlify, and GitHub Actions.

roles.title: Senior Software Engineer
responsibilities: Wrote the technical design and built the MVP for a B2B customer portal; developed a Lit component system and integrated customer feedback with Linear.

roles.title: Software Engineer
responsibilities: Integrated Router Limits technologies following acquisition and owned the Bark React Native app.

roles.title: Software Developer
responsibilities: Led frontend development; built an AngularJS progressive web app with a Node and MySQL REST API, plus Android and iOS apps using C# and Xamarin.Forms.

experience.company: Lockheed Martin Mission Systems and Training

roles.title: Software Engineer Intern
responsibilities: Contributed to training simulation software using C# .NET and WPF.

roles.title: Full Stack Programmer
responsibilities: Developed a chat application with Java Spring and an Oracle SQL backend.

skills.AI Software Factory: Slack integrations, automated Jira triage (JEV evaluation), scheduled triggers, GitLab CI/CD.
skills.Agent Orchestration: AgentOps, multi-agent orchestration, autonomous coding agents, Claude Code, Codex, Pi Harness, Cursor, Vercel AI SDK, LLM routing (LiteLLM, OpenRouter).
skills.MCP, Context and Memory: Model Context Protocol (MCP), FastMCP, MCP gateways, tool federation, context engineering, reusable agent skills, cross-session agent memory and retrieval.
skills.AI Governance: Microsoft Entra ID, role-based access control (RBAC), per-user OAuth, credential vaults, policy enforcement, fail-closed guardrails, human-in-the-loop approvals, audit trails.
skills.Agent Infrastructure: Kubernetes sandboxes, Docker, Argo CD, MinIO object storage, repository provisioning, Git credential proxies.
skills.Evaluation and Observability: Self-improvement loops, LLM evaluation (LLM-as-judge, replay), model and harness benchmarking, Playwright QA, test-driven development (TDD), independent agent code review, Datadog, AI cost and ROI tracking.

personalProject: Run a software factory with Claude and Codex workers across two development machines. Refine product ideas, prioritize tickets, and direct agents through test-first briefs, independent review, and controlled merges. Use failures to improve the workflow and package the practices for other engineers.
